turns.learner: Hello! Can you give me an exercise on comparatives (-er, more ... than)?
turns.tutor:
Let me show you one first: My brother is ___ (tall) than me.
Step 1: tall is a short word. Step 2: for a short word, I add -er, so tall becomes taller. Step 3: than comes next. Result: My brother is taller than me.
The rule: add -er to a short word, put more before a long word, then use than.
Right: A train is longer than a bus. Wrong: A train is more long than a bus.
Now you. Write the missing word.
Complete: "Cairo is ___ (big) than Luxor."
